advances: Conditional payment for prescribed closed traces on actual exposed fibers. It gives no automatic endpoint core or simultaneous decrease for unrestricted families.

proof:
Consider $K=K_p$ and $c=c_p$. By d90ba05577427854 choose the attained positive affine denominator $L(x)=1+a\cdot(x-c)$ minimizing $\int_KL^{-d-1}\,dx$. The image $K'$ under $T(x)=(x-c)/L(x)$ is a compact convex body, since the positive fractional-linear map and its inverse send segments to segments. Its Jacobian is $L^{-d-1}$. The first-moment identity of that fact gives $\int_{K'}u\,du=\int_K(x-c)L^{-d-2}\,dx=0$. In particular, by 6769574fc1bd9f8d with $m=|K'|$, every closed halfspace containing its centroid $0$ captures at least $\gamma_d|K'|$.

Let $\delta=\min_K L>0$ and let $f(t)$ agree with $t^{-d}$ on $[\delta,\infty)$ and with its tangent at $\delta$ on $(-\infty,\delta]$. This is finite, positive and convex on the real line. Define $\Psi(n,x)=h_{K-c}(n)f(L(x))$. The support factor is strictly positive and continuous for unit $n$, so $\Psi$ is finite continuous and convex in $x$ for each $n$. On $\partial K$ it is the outward flux of $F(x)=(x-c)L(x)^{-d}$, whose divergence is $dL(x)^{-d-1}$. For a through-$c$ halfspace its cutting plane has zero flux since $x-c$ is tangent. The plane cuts the interior, and its intersection with the old boundary is the relative boundary of the section and is surface-null. Gauss–Green therefore gives weighted old-boundary mass $d|K'\cap H'|$ for the corresponding central halfspace $H'$. The projective map preserves through-$c$ affine signs after translation since its denominator is positive. The whole-boundary mass is $d|K'|>0$. For $d=1$ this is the endpoint form of the same flux identity. Every closed halfspace containing $c$ contains its parallel through-$c$ halfspace, so the bound $\gamma_d$ also holds for that original trace, including whole-fiber traces.

For $p=0$ let $\ell(z)=-z$, and for $p=3$ let $\ell(z)=z-3$. The field $[\Psi(n,x)+B\ell(z)]_+$ agrees with $\Psi$ on the paying boundary and vanishes on the three others for a sufficiently large finite $B$, since their base gaps are strictly negative and $\Psi$ is bounded on the compact collection of marked boundaries. This field is convex in $(z,x)$ and jointly continuous. Each cap trace receives the bound separately, hence so does each probability mixture. Normalize the two denominators to one and add; the cross contributions are nonnegative, giving both asserted ratios.

statement:
Let positive compact convex $d$-bodies $K_0,K_1,K_2,K_3$, $d\ge1$, be actual sampled fibers over $0,1,2,3$. Take two finite nonempty ambient cap menus such that every trace of the first menu at $0$ contains one common point $c_0\in\operatorname{int}K_0$ and every trace of the second menu at $3$ contains one common point $c_3\in\operatorname{int}K_3$. The traces are closed and the chosen point can lie on their planes. Write $W_0,W_3$ for the probability-weighted closed-cap indicator profiles on the actual marked fiber boundaries, and let $\eta$ be their summed surface measure with endpoint counting for $d=1$. Put $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$.

For each $p\in\{0,3\}$ there is a globally finite nonnegative continuous field $\Phi_p(n,z,x)$, convex in the physical variables $(z,x)$ at each unit normal $n$, which vanishes on the other actual fiber boundaries and has $\int\Phi_p\,d\eta>0$. It satisfies $\int W_p\Phi_p\,d\eta\ge\gamma_d\int\Phi_p\,d\eta$ for every probability weighting of the relevant menu. After normalizing each denominator to one, their sum is one field of denominator two and pays at least $\gamma_d/2$ in ratio against each menu simultaneously.
title: A common interior endpoint trace gives a simultaneous boundary payment
